page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, with the printed page number 115 at the top right. Signature "h 2" at the foot, left of centre. Faint show-through marks in the right margin are left out.

main_text.p: rio iudicio eius maleficij, de quo inter sicarios quæritur, præiudicium fieri. Fieret autem hoc iudicio, quia si reus damnaretur, simul eum fuisse sicarium iudicaretur. F. At eiusmodi sunt iniuriæ, ut de his indignum sit, non primo quoque tempore iudicari. D. Atrocitas iniuriarum satisne causæ sit, quare dum de ea iudicetur, de aliquo maiore maleficio, de quo iudicium comparatum sit, præiudicetur. controuersiam iuris & æquitatis contentio peperit. Aliud tamen iuris postea fuisse, patet ex L. 4.D. de pub. iud. ubi Paulus ait,

page.notes: The running head reads "IVRISCONSVLTVS" with some ink overprint over the middle letters; the reading is the likely one. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout, so "sicarios", "fuisse" and "sit" appear where the scan shows an f-like long s. Line 8 shows a mark after "satis" that looks like an apostrophe; it is read as "satisne". The speaker labels "F." and "D." are kept inside the paragraph because they run on from the preceding lines without an indent. The final word "ait," ends the line and is not followed by a catchword.
